correctness.rationale: Independently quotient the eight microstates by global spin reversal: let p₀ be the stationary mass of the aligned class and p_i the mass of the class with odd spin i. Transitions 0→i, i→0 have rates (1−t_i)/2 and (1+t_i)/2; transitions between distinct odd-spin classes have rate 1/2. Stationarity and normalization give p_i=(1−t_i p₀)/(4+t_i) and p₀=[1−Σ_i 1/(4+t_i)]/[1−Σ_i t_i/(4+t_i)]. The nonzero energy changes at bath i are +4J out of the aligned class and −4J out of its own odd-spin class. Thus Q_i=2J[(1−t_i)p₀−(1+t_i)p_i]. Symbolic rational simplification reproduces every current and correlation in the record, with C_ij=1−2(p_i+p_j); all allowed rates are positive and Δ>25. Pair coefficients are positive and antisymmetric in the contribution to the two currents. A strict hot or cold extreme has the indicated sign; at equilibrium all currents vanish. For two distinct fixed other parameters the numerator is an affine decreasing function of t_i and changes sign exactly once between them. In the two placements, cancellation in the total hot currents gives the stated R. For D=8−xy−2y, 4/3−R=[8(1−y)+x(6−y)]/(3D); D stays positive and bounded on the closed parameter triangle. This proves the strict upper bound and that approaching equality requires x→0 and y→1; R>1 follows from y>x.
residual_risks: Current signs are strict for distinct extrema; tied equal temperatures have no pair flux between themselves. The sharp limit concerns the given bath placements at fixed positive J, not finite temperatures or other geometries.

evidence: The exact alternating Glauber chain solves all stationary correlations but expressly uses even N and two baths. The earlier two-temperature work is perturbative. The multibath extension of Lecomte et al. concerns a mean-field Hamiltonian and thermodynamic-limit solution, not a general finite triangle formula. Borchers et al. use conserved Kawasaki exchanges.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These are real prior stationary/heat-flow results; none was found to give a stronger solution specializing to arbitrary site temperatures in this finite odd ring. The N=3 mean-field Hamiltonian could be rescaled to match an equal triangle at the level of energies, but the inspected thermodynamic-limit formulas do not yield its exact finite state currents or sharp bound.

value.rationale: A symmetric closed triangle is a minimal three-terminal spin network, and its extra bond is precisely what separates it from the open three-spin rectifier. The positive pair law and unique balance setting quantify which reservoirs supply, absorb, or exchange zero net heat, beyond stationarity alone. The sharp bath-placement ratio supplies a fully normalized finite-model benchmark for rectification and its attainable limit, with no thermodynamic-limit claim.
residual_risks: The result does not extend the bound to larger rings, unequal couplings, other update clocks, or generic thermal devices.
